newsitem.title: UK: Skills shortage hits British business - survey.
newsitem.headline: Skills shortage hits British business - survey.

text.p: More than two-thirds of British business is suffering from a shortage of skilled employees, according to a survey published on Monday.
The report, published by recruitment firm Reed Personnel Services, found 68 percent of the 557 organisations it polled reported a shortage of skilled applicants for jobs.
"Skills shortages have clearly emerged as one of the most crucial issued facing UK businesses today," said Reed chairman Alec Reed.
"Rising requirements for multi-skilling across the board and increasing demand for new staff as the UK continues to recover from recession have all combined to create a major problem."
Economists have said a skills shortage could turn out to be a catalyst for a rise in inflation, at 2.9 percent in February.
Reed said the problem had been felt most in retail and the public sector, with 75 and 73 percent of respondents, respectively, claiming they have difficulty recruiting suitable employees.
